name: Teke-Laali
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Bissila, Sylvie-Blanche 1991. Description phonologique du ilaale (dialecte teke du Congo). Not online.

sources.citation: Jacquot, André. 1965. Précisions sur l'inventaire des langues teke du Congo. Cahiers d'Études africaines 5(18): 335-340. DOI 10.3406/cea.1965.3036
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Inventory/classification note on Teke varieties near Brazzaville (Fuumu etc.); all 6 pages of Persée scanned text downloaded. Does not mention Laali at all (its 'laadi' hits are Kongo Laadi H16f) and says nothing about accent/tone/stress.

sources.citation: Trézenem, Édouard. 1940. Contribution à l'étude des nègres africains: les Bateke Balali. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 10: 1-63. DOI 10.3406/jafr.1940.2484
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Physical-anthropology and ethnography of the Balali (= Laali) Teke; all 63 pages of Persée scanned text downloaded (PDF is behind an altcha captcha). No section on language; no mention of accent, tone or stress (only one lexical aside, 'Bake signifie en dialecte kiteke « les tout petits »').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page teke1277 (Hammarström et al.), https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/teke1277
sources.note: Lists only the two Brazzaville theses as descriptive references plus subclassification refs (Pacchiarotti et al. 2019, Mouandza 2002, Kristensen/Webster/Webster 1984); nothing on stress.
Stub: Laali is one of four varieties of the West Teke dialect continuum (Tsaayi, Laali, Yaa, Tyee); cites only Ethnologue and Maho 2009; no phonology.

sources.citation: Bouka, Léonce Yembi. 1989. Teke and its dialects in Congo: status of the research. In T. G. Bergman (ed.), Proceedings of the round table on assuring the feasibility of standardization within dialect chains, 63-75. Nairobi: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL overview of the Congo Teke dialect chain including Ilaali; may summarize prosodic (tone/accent) properties of the West Teke varieties. Once an open SIL PDF (repository/), now dead; SIL archive search could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Leblanc, Simon. 2012. Le développement des langues de la République du Congo: état des travaux. Brazzaville: SIL Groupe Afrique centrale-Congo. 138 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL Congo bibliographical survey; would list any SIL Laali phonology/orthography sketches produced after 1991 (e.g. by R. Raharimanantsoa, who did Eboo and SW Teke).

sources.citation: Moussoua, Chanderlin Frédéric. 2005. Aspects of morphological variations in the word formation process in "Laale", a dialect of the "Teke" language. MA thesis, Université Marien Ngouabi, Brazzaville.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Second Laali-specific thesis; an English-language morphology thesis normally opens with a phonology chapter (tone, possibly accent).

sources.citation: Mouandza, Jean-Daniel. 2002. Éléments de description du iyaa (parler bantu du Congo-Brazzaville). Thèse de doctorat, Université de Nice-Sophia Antipolis.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Full description of Yaa (iyx, B73c), the closest sister variety in the same West Teke continuum (Nzebi-Laali-Yaa clade); would give the continuum-level prosodic picture (tone, absence/presence of accent) if nothing Laali-specific can be obtained — not a Laali source.

sources.citation: Bissila, Sylvie-Blanche. 1991. Description phonologique du ilaale (dialecte téké du Congo). Mémoire de maîtrise, Université Marien Ngouabi, Brazzaville. 138 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The only full phonological description of Laali on record (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology, hh:phon:Bissila:Laale); a 138-page French phonology thesis would treat tone and almost certainly say whether there is an accent/stress.

sources.citation: Kristensen, Ole-Bjørn, Don Webster & Thelma Webster. 1984. Enquête dialectale Teke. 16 pp. SIL ms.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL dialect survey covering Ilaali; may contain a brief phonological note on tone/accent for each variety.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana. London: Church Missionary House. ('Mutsaya' wordlist = Laali B73b mixed with Kongo, per Glottolog language code note)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Glottolog/Welmers note: Koelle 'marked what he heard as stress' but 'failed to recognize tone'; a comparative wordlist, gives no rule. Not opened.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 87-162. (Glottolog ref 586272)
sources.note: Lexicostatistic classification; not on Persée (collection ends at vol. 21/2015), UGent biblio search returned HTTP 500. Not expected to discuss stress.
